citations.title: Applicability
citations.requirement: Chapter 6400 applicability. The Department inspects a sample of an agency's homes serving 8 or fewer each year. Each home serving 9 or more is inspected annually (per research summary; subsection text not re-read).

citations.title: Licensure or approval of facilities and agencies
citations.requirement: A certificate of compliance is required before a community home operates. Applies to for-profit and nonprofit homes (per research summary).

citations.title: Maximum capacity
citations.requirement: The certificate states each home's location and maximum capacity. The stated capacity may not be exceeded (per research summary).

citations.title: Fire safety occupancy permit
citations.requirement: Each home must hold a fire safety occupancy permit (certificate of occupancy) from the local building or fire authority (per ODP guide in research).

citations.title: Self-assessment of homes
citations.requirement: Section governs agency self-assessment of its homes. Detail not retrieved; confirm frequency and form in the rule text.

citations.title: Abuse
citations.requirement: Section governs abuse of individuals. The manual's abuse and neglect policy must implement it. Detail not retrieved; confirm in the rule text.

citations.title: Child abuse
citations.requirement: Section governs child abuse. Per ODP guide, Child Protective Services Law clearances apply if anyone 17 or younger lives in the home. Confirm detail in the rule text.

citations.title: Incident report and investigation
citations.requirement: Listed incidents require an incident report and investigation. A staff person must report within 24 hours of discovery (per ODP guide in research).

citations.title: Incident procedures to protect the individual
citations.requirement: Section sets procedures to protect the individual after an incident. Detail not retrieved; confirm in the rule text.

citations.title: Incident analysis
citations.requirement: Section requires analysis of incidents (trend and prevention review). Detail not retrieved; confirm frequency in the rule text.

citations.title: Criminal history record check
citations.requirement: PA State Police check application due within 5 working days after hire. FBI check for non-PA residents. Results must be evaluated; the old lifetime-ban list cannot bar hire after Peake (per ODP guide).

citations.title: Individual funds and property
citations.requirement: Section governs management and protection of individual funds and property. Detail not retrieved; confirm account, records and accounting rules in the rule text.

citations.title: Grievance procedures
citations.requirement: The home must have a grievance procedure for individuals. Detail not retrieved; confirm timelines and notice content in the rule text.

citations.title: Exercise of rights
citations.requirement: Section governs how an individual exercises rights, including through a family member or advocate. Detail not retrieved; confirm in the rule text.

citations.title: Rights of the individual
citations.requirement: Lists the individual's rights in the home. The rights policy must track the enumerated list; confirm each item in the rule text.

citations.title: Negotiation of choices
citations.requirement: Section governs negotiation of conflicting choices among individuals. Detail not retrieved; confirm in the rule text.

citations.title: Informing of rights
citations.requirement: Individuals must be informed of their rights. Detail not retrieved; confirm timing, format and acknowledgment in the rule text.

citations.title: Minimum age
citations.requirement: Minimum staff age. Staff counted in staffing ratios must be 18 or older (per ODP guide in research).

citations.title: Chief executive officer
citations.requirement: One CEO is required: a master's degree plus 2 years, or a bachelor's degree plus 4 years, of administration or human-services experience (per ODP guide).

citations.title: Program specialist
citations.requirement: One program specialist per 30 individuals. Bachelor's plus 2 years of ID/autism experience, or master's plus 1 year, or associate/60 credits plus 4 years (per ODP guide).

citations.title: Staffing
citations.requirement: Minimum 1 staff per 8 individuals awake and present, and 1 per 16 while individuals sleep (§6400.45(b)). Staffing in each individual plan must be implemented as written (§6400.45(d)).

citations.title: Emergency training
citations.requirement: Per ODP guide: first aid, Heimlich and CPR training within 6 months after hire and annually after. Keep certificates in the personnel file.

citations.title: Training records
citations.requirement: Section requires records of staff training. Detail not retrieved; confirm required content and retention in the rule text.

citations.title: Orientation
citations.requirement: Per ODP guide: required orientation is completed before working alone with individuals and within 30 days after hire.

citations.title: Annual training
citations.requirement: Per ODP guide: 24 hours a year for direct service workers, supervisors and program specialists. 12 hours a year for management, administrative and fiscal staff.

citations.title: Unobstructed egress
citations.requirement: Exits and egress routes must be kept unobstructed. Detail not retrieved; confirm in the rule text.

citations.title: Evacuation procedures
citations.requirement: The home must have written evacuation procedures, including routes tailored to residents' mobility. Detail not retrieved; confirm posting and content in the rule text.

citations.title: Smoke detectors and fire alarms
citations.requirement: Smoke detectors and fire alarms must be installed and maintained. Detail not retrieved; confirm locations and testing frequency in the rule text.

citations.title: Fire drills
citations.requirement: Per ODP guide: an unannounced fire drill at least monthly, and a drill during sleeping hours at least every 6 months. Record each drill and correct problems found.

citations.title: Individual physical examination
citations.requirement: Per ODP guide: each individual needs a physical examination within 12 months before admission and annually after.

citations.title: Health services
citations.requirement: Section governs health services for individuals. Detail not retrieved; confirm in the rule text.

citations.title: Emergency medical plan
citations.requirement: The home must maintain an emergency medical plan. Detail not retrieved; confirm required content in the rule text.

citations.title: Self-administration
citations.requirement: Section governs self-administration of medication by individuals. Detail not retrieved; confirm assessment and support requirements in the rule text.

citations.title: Medication administration
citations.requirement: Section governs who may administer medication and how. Detail not retrieved; confirm in the rule text.

citations.title: Storage and disposal of medications
citations.requirement: Section governs safe storage and disposal of medications. Detail not retrieved; confirm in the rule text.

citations.title: Prescription medications
citations.requirement: Section governs prescription medications, including administration as prescribed. Detail not retrieved; confirm in the rule text.

citations.title: Medication record
citations.requirement: A medication record must be kept for each individual. Detail not retrieved; confirm required entries in the rule text.

citations.title: Medication errors
citations.requirement: Section governs response to and reporting of medication errors. Detail not retrieved; confirm in the rule text.

citations.title: Medication administration training
citations.requirement: Staff who administer medications must complete medication administration training. Detail not retrieved; confirm course, recertification and observation rules in the rule text.

citations.title: Definition of restrictive procedures
citations.requirement: Defines restrictive procedures for Chapter 6400. The restrictive-intervention policy must use this definition. Detail not retrieved; confirm in the rule text.

citations.title: Written policy
citations.requirement: Section requires a written policy on restrictive procedures. Detail not retrieved; confirm required content in the rule text.

citations.title: Human rights team
citations.requirement: Section governs a human rights team's review of restrictive procedures. Detail not retrieved; confirm membership and review frequency in the rule text.

citations.title: Behavior support component of the individual plan
citations.requirement: Behavior support must be a component of the individual plan. Detail not retrieved; confirm required elements in the rule text.

citations.title: Staff training
citations.requirement: Staff training is required in the home's restrictive-procedure and behavior-support policy. Detail not retrieved; confirm required topics and timing in the rule text.

citations.title: Prohibited procedures
citations.requirement: Lists procedures that are prohibited in the home. The policy must reproduce the prohibited list exactly; confirm each item in the rule text.

citations.title: Physical restraint
citations.requirement: Section governs physical restraint. Detail not retrieved; confirm permitted use, limits and documentation in the rule text.

citations.title: Emergency use of a physical restraint
citations.requirement: Section governs emergency use of physical restraint. Detail not retrieved; confirm conditions, duration, notification and follow-up in the rule text.

citations.title: Access to or the use of an individual's personal property
citations.requirement: Section limits restricting access to, or use of, an individual's personal property. Detail not retrieved; confirm conditions in the rule text.

citations.title: Emergency information
citations.requirement: Emergency information must be kept for each individual. Detail not retrieved; confirm required items in the rule text.

citations.title: Individual records
citations.requirement: A record must be kept for each individual. Detail not retrieved; confirm in the rule text.

citations.title: Content of records
citations.requirement: Specifies required contents of each individual record. Build the record checklist from this section; confirm each item in the rule text.

citations.title: Record retention
citations.requirement: Sets how long individual records are retained. The retention period was not retrieved; confirm the period in the rule text before stating it in the manual.

citations.title: Access
citations.requirement: Governs who may access individual records. Detail not retrieved; confirm in the rule text.

citations.title: Release of information
citations.requirement: Governs release of information from individual records. Detail not retrieved; confirm consent requirements in the rule text.

citations.title: Application form
citations.requirement: Apply on the Department-prescribed form, one application per home. The entity may not operate until notified that a certificate of compliance will issue (per research).

citations.title: Room and board rate
citations.requirement: Room and board charge may not exceed the regulatory cap, and the individual keeps the personal needs allowance (per research). Confirm the current formula with ODP.

citations.title: Room and board agreement
citations.requirement: A Room and Board Agreement is required for each individual receiving residential habilitation (per research, using ODP Attachment 4). Section text not re-read.

citations.title: Room and Board for Individuals Enrolled in ODP
citations.requirement: Form DP 1077 is mandatory: before admission, annually, and within 15 days of an emergency placement. Increases that cut personal funds need 30 days' written notice. No room and board during respite.

citations.title: Chapter 6400 Regulatory Compliance Guide
citations.requirement: ODP's plain-language guide to capacity, physical plant, staff qualifications, training, background checks, fire drills and incident reporting. It also covers regulatory waiver requests to ra-odplicensing@pa.gov after 30 days' notice to individuals.

policies.title: Licensure, Certificate of Compliance and Licensed Capacity
state_specifics: Certificate of compliance is required before any individual is admitted. One application per home, filed on the Department form (HS-633).
Do not operate until notified that a certificate will issue.
Never exceed the maximum capacity on the certificate. Amend the certificate before changing a home's size or location.
Licensing and ODP provider enrollment are separate gates; a certificate alone does not authorize payment.
The Department inspects a sample of homes serving 8 or fewer each year; each home serving 9 or more is inspected annually.

policies.title: Annual Department Inspection and Agency Self-Assessment
state_specifics: Use the ODP Chapter 6400 Regulatory Compliance Guide as the self-inspection checklist.
Confirm self-assessment frequency and form in the §6400.15 rule text before finalizing.
Audit personnel files, training hours, fire drills, incident reports, physical exams and room and board agreements quarterly.
Correct and document every finding on a written plan of correction.

policies.title: Abuse Prohibition, Prevention and Child Abuse Reporting
state_specifics: Abuse (§6400.16) includes striking, neglect, rape, sexual molestation, exploitation or harassment, staff-individual sexual contact, restraint outside chapter rules, financial exploitation, humiliation and withholding regularly scheduled meals.
Report abuse or suspected abuse of an individual 17 or younger immediately to ChildLine, 1-800-932-0313 (§6400.17).
Abuse is also a 24-hour incident reportable in the Department's information management system (§6400.18).
Child Protective Services Law clearances apply only if anyone 17 or younger lives in the home.
Staff are trained in prevention, detection and reporting under OAPSA, CPSL and the Adult Protective Services Act.

policies.title: Incident Reporting and Notification
state_specifics: Report within 24 hours of staff discovery: death, suicide attempt, inpatient admission, abuse, neglect, exploitation, missing more than 24 hours or in jeopardy, law enforcement activity, injury beyond first aid, fire needing the fire department (not false alarms), emergency closure, theft or misuse of funds, rights violation.
Report within 72 hours: use of restraint, and a medication error if the medication was ordered by a health care practitioner (§6400.167).
Notify the individual and persons they designate within 24 hours of discovery. Keep documentation of the notice.
The incident report or summary of findings and actions is available on request to the individual and designees, redacted of other individuals' information and the reporter.
Finalize the report within 30 days of discovery unless the Department is notified in writing of the need for an extension and the reason.

policies.title: Incident Response and Certified Incident Investigation
state_specifics: Take immediate action to protect the individual's health, safety and well-being upon first knowledge of an incident, alleged incident or suspected incident.
Initiate an investigation within 24 hours of discovery.

A Department-certified incident investigator is required for: death during service, hospital admission from an accidental, unexplained or staff/individual/restraint-caused injury, abuse, neglect, exploitation, injury beyond first aid with those causes, theft or misuse of funds, and rights violations.
Maintain access to a Certified Investigator at all times and name the primary and backup investigators.

policies.title: Incident Analysis and Trend Review
state_specifics: Review and analyze incidents and document a trend analysis at least every 3 months.
For each confirmed incident, document cause analysis, corrective action and a risk-reduction strategy.
Document preventive measures, educate staff and the individual, and monitor incidents to mitigate and manage risk (§6400.20(a), (c)-(e)).
Results feed the quality improvement and mortality review policy.

policies.title: Criminal History Record Checks and Hiring Decisions
state_specifics: Submit the PA State Police application for every prospective direct-contact employee, including part-time and temporary staff, within 5 working days after hire.
Non-PA residents also need an FBI check within 5 working days after hire.
Checks must be completed no more than 1 year before the hire date.
Per ODP guide, OAPSA standards supersede these timeframes; request checks on or before the first day of work.
Make and document a case-by-case hiring decision when a record exists. The former lifetime-ban list cannot be used to bar hire after Peake.

policies.title: Individual Funds and Property Protection and Accounting
state_specifics: Written procedures must protect funds and personal property and provide for adequate accounting.
Procedures must include counseling each individual on the use of funds and property based on that person's needs.
The policy may not prohibit an individual's right to manage their own finances.
Reference the §6400.22(b)-(g) provisions (account, records, commingling) after confirming each in the rule text.
Theft or misuse of individual funds is a 24-hour reportable incident requiring a certified investigator.

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Written grievance procedures must cover individuals, families, advocates and staff and ensure investigation and resolution of complaints.
Waiver providers also have Chapter 6100 complaint requirements (§6100.51); confirm text before finalizing.
Confirm timelines and notice content in the §6400.23 rule text.
Prohibit retaliation. A rights violation is also a 24-hour reportable incident.

policies.title: Rights of the Individual and Informing of Rights
state_specifics: Explain individual rights and how to report a rights violation to the individual and designees upon admission and annually.
Keep the signed acknowledgment (§6400.34(b)).
Rights policy must track every item enumerated in §6400.32.
Provide rights information in the individual's preferred communication format.

policies.title: Exercise of Rights, Rights Restrictions, Due Process and Informed Consent
state_specifics: Individuals may exercise rights directly or through a family member or advocate (§6400.31).
Any restriction of access to or use of personal property follows §6400.210 and the restrictive procedures policy.
HCBS settings rule: modifications need an assessed need, a plan entry, informed consent and periodic review.
Support decision-making; do not assume incapacity. Document consent and who consented.

policies.title: Negotiation of Choices Among Individuals
state_specifics: Assist affected individuals to negotiate choices following the home's written procedures for resolving differences (§6400.33(b)).
Procedures describe how differences are resolved and how choice is promoted and protected without significant health and safety risk.
Procedures may not violate any individual's rights.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Records are accessible only to those authorized under §6400.216.
Release information only with consent under §6400.217. Confirm consent content in the rule text.
Appoint a privacy officer, provide a notice of privacy practices and train all staff.
Breach notification follows 45 CFR 164.400-414.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Communication Access
state_specifics: Provide interpreters, auxiliary aids and translated materials at no cost.
Admission and services may not discriminate on disability type, race, national origin or religion.
Document each individual's communication method in the plan.

policies.title: Chief Executive Officer and Program Specialist Qualifications
state_specifics: CEO: master's plus 2 years, or bachelor's plus 4 years, of administration or human-services experience.
ODP waiver enrollment separately requires an executive with a bachelor's and 5 years' residential management experience.
One program specialist per 30 individuals: bachelor's plus 2 years of ID/autism experience, master's plus 1 year, or associate/60 credits plus 4 years.
Keep job descriptions and an organizational chart in personnel files.

policies.title: Staffing Ratios, Supervision and Awake Overnight Staff
state_specifics: Minimum 1 staff per 8 individuals while awake and present; 1 per 16 while individuals sleep (§6400.45(b)).
Staffing and qualifications in each individual plan must be implemented as written, even above minimums (§6400.45(d)).
Staff counted in ratios must be 18 or older (§6400.42).
Do not assume sleep-shift status; confirm the §6400.232 awake-staff requirement for each home type.
Maintain an on-call and backup coverage roster so no shift falls below the ratio.

policies.title: Staff Orientation Program
state_specifics: Complete orientation before working alone with individuals and within 30 days of hire.
Orientation covers person-centered practices, community integration, choice and relationships.

It also covers prevention, detection and reporting of abuse under OAPSA, CPSL and the Adult Protective Services Act, plus individual rights, recognizing and reporting incidents, and job-related knowledge and skills.
Keep sign-in sheets and the curriculum.

policies.title: Annual Staff Training Plan
state_specifics: 24 hours a year for direct service workers, supervisors and program specialists; 12 hours for management, administrative and fiscal staff.
Establish the training-year dates in writing.
Topics must include person-centered practices, abuse prevention and reporting, rights, incident recognition and reporting.
For direct workers, also cover safe use of behavior supports and implementation of the individual plan.

policies.title: Fire Safety, First Aid, Heimlich and CPR Training
state_specifics: Program specialists and direct service workers are trained before working with individuals in general fire safety, evacuation, drill responsibilities and the outside meeting place.
Training also covers smoking safety if anyone smokes at the home, extinguishers, smoke detectors and alarms, and notifying the fire department promptly.
Fire safety training is repeated annually (§6400.46(b)).
First aid, Heimlich and CPR training is due within 6 months of hire and annually. Keep certificates in the personnel file.

policies.title: Personnel and Training Records
state_specifics: Maintain a training record per employee under §6400.50. Confirm required content and retention.
Keep hire date, orientation, annual hours, CPR/first aid dates, TB documentation and background check dates.
Review a training tracker monthly.
Keep job descriptions and qualifications evidence for CEO, program specialist and direct support staff.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Staff-individual sexual contact is abuse under §6400.16.
Prohibit financial dealings, gifts, loans and use of individual property by staff.
Staff are mandated to report suspected abuse.
Violations lead to discipline up to termination and a report to the Department.

policies.title: Residential Environment, Bedrooms, Bathrooms and Accessibility
state_specifics: No more than 2 individuals sleep in a bedroom.
A single bedroom needs at least 80 sq ft; shared rooms need 60 sq ft per person.
1 toilet per 4 individuals; a home with one tub/shower cannot exceed capacity of 4.
Provider supplies basic cable, basic internet, a landline that works during a power outage, bedding, towels and toiletries.
Match accessibility modifications to each person's needs with landlord consent.

policies.title: Transportation and Vehicle Safety
state_specifics: No verified Chapter 6400 section was identified for this topic; confirm any applicable rule in the rule text.
Require valid license, insurance and registration, and background clearances for drivers.
Drivers know the emergency medical plan, seat belt and wheelchair securement use.
Report vehicle incidents under the incident policy.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Bloodborne pathogen exposure control plan and Hepatitis B vaccine offer for staff with exposure risk.
Standard precautions, handwashing, laundry and sharps handling.
Staff illness exclusion and notification of public health authorities as required.
Supply cleaning products and personal protective equipment.

policies.title: Fire Safety Occupancy Permit, Egress, Smoke Detectors and Inoperative-Alarm Monitoring
state_specifics: Hold a fire safety occupancy permit from the local authority for each home (§6400.14).
Keep exits and egress routes unobstructed (§6400.101).
Install, maintain and test smoke detectors and alarms (§6400.110). Confirm locations and test frequency in the rule text.
Written procedure for fire safety monitoring if a smoke detector or fire alarm is inoperative (§6400.110(h)).
Equip with fire extinguishers; inspect and log.

policies.title: Emergency Evacuation Procedures and Emergency Preparedness
state_specifics: Written evacuation procedures include individual and staff responsibilities, means of transportation and an emergency shelter location.
Tailor evacuation steps to each resident's mobility.
Plan for loss of power, heat, water or staff and keep emergency contact lists.

policies.title: Fire Drills
state_specifics: Hold an unannounced fire drill at least monthly.
Hold a drill during sleeping hours at least every 6 months.
Record each drill and correct problems found.
Rotate drill times and exits.

policies.title: Smoking Safety
state_specifics: If an individual or staff person smokes at the home, written smoking safety procedures are required (§6400.114(a), per RCG p.88).
The procedures must be followed (§6400.114(b)).
If no one smokes at the home, document that.
Include smoking safety in staff fire safety training.

policies.title: Physical Examinations, Health Services and Refusal of Care
state_specifics: Each individual needs a physical examination within 12 months before admission and annually after.
If an individual refuses routine medical or dental care, document the refusal and continued attempts to train them on the need for health care in the record (§6400.143(a)).
Procedures for managing refusals are reviewed by licensing staff.
Support access to health care per §6400.144; confirm text.

policies.title: Emergency Medical Plan and Change of Condition
state_specifics: Written emergency medical plan lists the hospital or source of health care, the method of transportation and an emergency staffing plan.
The plan is person-specific.
Staff notify the nurse or health care practitioner and responsible persons of condition changes.
Inpatient hospital admission is a 24-hour reportable incident.

policies.title: Nursing Oversight, Health Monitoring, Seizures and Choking Risk
state_specifics: Document health risks, seizure plans and choking or dysphagia protocols in the individual plan.
Train staff on each person's protocols before working alone.
Confirm any MCC-related qualification requirements in ODPANN 26-044 when serving individuals with a Medically Complex Condition.
Coordinate with practitioners and supports coordinator.

policies.title: Death of an Individual
state_specifics: Death is a 24-hour reportable incident.
A certified incident investigator investigates a death during service.
Notify designated persons within 24 hours.
Feeds mortality review.

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
state_specifics: No verified Chapter 6400 staff health section citation was identified; confirm the staff health requirements and TB screening rules in the rule text before finalizing.
Keep records in the personnel file.
Exclude ill staff per the infection control policy.
Offer Hepatitis B vaccine where occupational exposure is possible.

policies.title: Medication Administration, Self-Administration and Staff Certification
state_specifics: Assess and support self-administration (§6400.161).
Only staff who completed medication administration training administer medications (§6400.169). Confirm course, recertification and observation rules.
Administer prescription medications as prescribed (§6400.165).
Staff must know medication errors reporting rules.

policies.title: Medication Storage and Disposal
state_specifics: Discontinued or expired prescription medications are destroyed safely per federal and state law (§6400.163(h)).
Document each disposal.
Store medications securely per §6400.163.

policies.title: Medication Records and Medication Errors
state_specifics: Maintain a medication record for each individual (§6400.166).
Report medication errors involving practitioner-ordered medications within 72 hours.
Notify the practitioner and designated persons.
Review errors in quarterly incident analysis.

policies.title: Food, Nutrition, Menus and Modified Diets
state_specifics: Never withhold regularly scheduled meals; this is abuse under §6400.16.
Prescribed modified diets and texture requirements are written in the plan and followed.
Individuals choose meals. Written menu rules at §6400.243 are mandatory only in homes serving 9 or more.
Supply food preparation labor and kitchen sanitation.

policies.title: Referral, Admission and Transition In
state_specifics: Admissions flow through the supports coordinator, the individual's team and the county administrative entity.
Physical exam within 12 months before admission is required.
Complete Form DP 1077 before admission.
Confirm that bedroom sharing, ratio and capacity fit the individual before move-in.

policies.title: Person-Centered Plan, Behavior Support Component and Daily Documentation
state_specifics: Implement staffing and qualifications in each individual plan as written (§6400.45(d)).
Behavior support must be a component of the plan (§6400.195).
Document daily service delivery for billing and monitoring.
Program specialist oversees plan implementation.

policies.title: Community Integration and Employment Choice
state_specifics: Support access to community, employment, relationships and visitors without restriction not in the plan.
Staff are trained in community integration at orientation and annually.
Document choices and offers.

policies.title: Transition, Discharge and Termination of Services
state_specifics: Coordinate with the supports coordinator and team; provide advance notice and appeal information.
Board charges stop on the 8th consecutive day of leave or hospitalization; room stops after 30 consecutive hospital days.
Transfer records and funds per consent.
Report emergency closure as an incident.

policies.title: Missing Person and Elopement
state_specifics: Report as an incident within 24 hours if missing more than 24 hours or if the person could be in jeopardy if missing at all.
Immediately search and notify law enforcement and designated persons if in jeopardy.
Include an elopement risk plan in the individual plan.

policies.title: Restrictive Procedures Policy, Human Rights Team and Property Restrictions
state_specifics: Written agency-wide and individual-specific policy defines prohibition or use of restrictive procedures, circumstances, who may authorize, and a monitoring and control mechanism (§6400.192).
Use the §6400.191 definition of restrictive procedures.
A human rights team reviews restrictive procedures (§6400.194). Confirm membership and frequency.
Limits on restricting personal property follow §6400.210.
If all restrictive procedures are prohibited, say so.

policies.title: Prohibited Procedures, Physical Restraint and Emergency Restraint
state_specifics: Reproduce the §6400.207 prohibited list exactly.
Physical restraint follows §6400.208 and emergency use §6400.209. Confirm limits and documentation.
Restraint is reported within 72 hours and is an abuse indicator if outside chapter rules.
Debrief and review each use.

policies.title: Positive Behavior Support and Staff Training
state_specifics: Behavior support is a plan component (§6400.195).
Train staff in the restrictive procedures and behavior support policy (§6400.196).
Annual training includes safe and appropriate use of behavior supports.
Use least-restrictive, positive approaches first.

policies.title: Individual Records, Content and Emergency Information
state_specifics: Keep a record for each individual (§6400.212).
Build the record checklist from §6400.213.
Maintain current emergency information (§6400.211).
Include physical exam, plan, medication record and Room and Board Agreement.

policies.title: Record Retention, Access and Release of Information
state_specifics: Retention period is set in §6400.215; confirm it in the rule text before stating a number.
Access limited under §6400.216; release only per §6400.217.
Menu retention of 3 months applies only to homes serving 9 or more.

policies.category: Home Serving Nine or More Individuals
policies.title: Posted Evacuation Procedures and Diagram (Homes Serving 9+)
state_specifics: Applies only to homes serving nine or more individuals (§6400.236).
Post written evacuation procedures per §6400.103 and an evacuation diagram showing egress direction in a conspicuous place.
Update diagrams when layout changes.
State in the manual when the home serves 8 or fewer and the section does not apply.

policies.category: Home Serving Nine or More Individuals
policies.title: Written Daily Menus (Homes Serving 9+)
state_specifics: Applies only to homes serving nine or more (§6400.243).
Prepare a written daily menu accessible to individuals at least 1 day before the menu date.
Make changes accessible in advance of the meal, and follow the written menu and changes.
Retain written menus at least 3 months.

policies.title: Emergency Placement
state_specifics: Never exceed licensed capacity, including for emergency placements.
Complete Form DP 1077 within 15 days of an emergency placement.
Obtain emergency information and a physical exam record as soon as possible; confirm timelines in the rule text.
Notify the supports coordinator at once.

policies.title: Respite Care
state_specifics: Do not charge room and board during respite.
Respite individuals count toward licensed capacity and staffing ratios.
Confirm respite rules in the Chapter 6400 respite section before offering the service.

policies.title: Governing Body, Provider Enrollment, Policy Review and Regulatory Waivers
state_specifics: ODP provider enrollment is separate from licensure; new residential providers enroll via competitive RFA since 1/1/2025.
Review policies at least annually and keep version history.
Regulatory waiver requests go to ra-odplicensing@pa.gov after 30 days' notice to affected individuals.
Residential performance standards effective 1/1/2026 drive Select and Clinically Enhanced status.
Name the legal entity exactly as on the application.

policies.title: Quality Improvement, Data Review and Mortality Review
state_specifics: Review incident trends at least every 3 months.
Track ODP residential performance measures.
Review all deaths and report outcomes to the governing body.

policies.title: Medicaid Compliance, Billing and Service Documentation
state_specifics: ODP is the effective single payer; fee schedule rates are maximums set by ODP.
Reconcile billed days to attendance monthly.
Confirm with ODP whether EVV applies to community-home Residential Habilitation.
Confirm billing procedure codes (for example W9000) and the delivery system with ODP.

policies.title: Room and Board Agreements and Personal Needs Allowance
state_specifics: A Room and Board Agreement (Form DP 1077) is required before admission, annually and within 15 days of an emergency placement.
Charge may not exceed 72% of SSI plus State Supplement, 40% for room only, 32% for board only, or documented actual cost.
Give 30 days' written notice of increases that reduce personal funds.
Individuals keep the personal needs allowance; no room and board during respite.
2026 SSI federal rate is $994/month; confirm the current State Supplement with ODP.

forms.name: Incident Report (Department information management system)

documents.title: 55 Pa. Code Chapter 6400 Regulatory Compliance Guide (RCG) – Community Homes for Individuals with an Intellectual Disability or Autism
documents.form_number: None (companion to 55 Pa. Code Ch. 6400; Appendix A is the Self-Assessment Licensing Inspection Instrument)
documents.issuer: PA DHS Office of Developmental Programs (ODP), Regulatory Administration / Licensing
documents.version: March 15, 2023 Edition. This is the current edition on the MyODP Licensing page, and it replaces the Feb. 3, 2020 edition listed in the regulations input.
documents.how_used: No single policy checklist could be read, so this is the fallback the task allows. The RCG reproduces each 6400 regulation verbatim, with ODP's discussion and the inspection procedures licensing staff use. I pulled every provision that requires a written policy, procedure or plan (Part A). I also pulled provisions that the RCG says licensing staff check through 'applicable policies' (Part B). Item numbering follows the RCG, e.g. '22a', '110h', '243a-e'.

documents.title: NEW 6400 Policy Review List – Community Homes for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities
documents.issuer: PA DHS ODP (posted on MyODP Licensing and Regulations page, dated 29 Mar 2022)
documents.how_used: This looks like the official new-applicant policy review document. The file came back as compressed binary, so I could not read its items and did not use it to build the list. The applicant should download it and reconcile it against the items below. Where it uses its own numbering or order, that should override this list. The MyODP page also lists a 'Checklist for the Initial Application (Appendix A)' and a 'New Applicant Licensing Flow Chart'.

required_items.text: There shall be a written policy that establishes procedures for the protection and adequate accounting of individual funds and property and for counseling the individual concerning the use of funds and property.
required_items.cite: RCG p.33; 55 Pa. Code §6400.22(a). The RCG says the policy must show how it protects funds, protects personal property, and specifies counseling based on each individual's needs, and strongly recommends referencing 22b-22g.

required_items.text: The home's policy may not prohibit the individual's right to manage the individual's own finances.
The home shall have written grievance procedures for individuals, individual's families, advocates, and staff persons that assure investigation and resolution of complaints.
required_items.cite: RCG p.35; §6400.23. Waiver providers also have Ch. 6100.51(a)-(h) complaint requirements, which I did not read.

required_items.text: The provider shall assist the affected individuals to negotiate choices in accordance with the provider's procedures for the individuals to resolve differences and make choices.
required_items.cite: RCG p.51; §6400.33(b). The RCG says the procedures must describe how differences are resolved, how choice is promoted and protected without significant health and safety risk, and must not violate any rights.

required_items.text: There shall be written emergency evacuation procedures that include individual and staff responsibilities, means of transportation and an emergency shelter location.
There shall be a written procedure for fire safety monitoring in the event the smoke detector or fire alarm is inoperative.
If an individual or staff person smokes at the home, there shall be written smoking safety procedures.
required_items.cite: RCG p.88; §6400.114(a). 114b requires the procedures to be followed.

required_items.text: The home shall have a written emergency medical plan listing the following: 1. The hospital or source of health care that will be used in an emergency. 2. The method of transportation to be used. An emergency staffing plan.
required_items.cite: RCG p.93; §6400.145. The RCG says the plan is person-specific.

required_items.text: The home shall develop and implement a written policy that defines the prohibition or use of specific types of restrictive procedures, describes the circumstances in which restrictive procedures may be used, the staff persons who may authorize the use of restrictive procedures, and a mechanism to monitor and control the use of restrictive procedures.
required_items.cite: RCG p.124; §6400.192. The RCG says the policy must be agency-wide and individual-specific and address all elements of the Restrictive Procedures section unless the agency forbids all restrictive procedures.

required_items.text: Written emergency evacuation procedures as specified in §6400.103 (relating to evacuation procedures) and an evacuation diagram specifying direction for egress in the event of an emergency, shall be posted in a conspicuous place.
required_items.cite: RCG p.129; §6400.236. Applies only to homes serving nine or more individuals.

required_items.text: (a) A written daily menu shall be prepared and accessible to an individual. (b) The menu shall be accessible to an individual at least 1 day prior to the menu date. (c) A change to a menu shall be accessible to an individual in advance of the meal. (d) A written menu and changes to the menu shall be followed. (e) A written menu shall be retained for at least 3 months.
required_items.cite: RCG p.130; §6400.243. Applies only to homes serving nine or more individuals.

required_items.text: Abuse of an individual is prohibited. Abuse is an act or omission of an act that willfully deprives an individual of rights or human dignity or which may cause or causes actual physical injury or emotional harm to an individual, such as striking or kicking an individual; neglect; rape; sexual molestation, sexual exploitation, or sexual harassment of an individual; sexual contact between a staff person and an individual; restraining an individual without following the requirements in this chapter; financial exploitation of an individual; humiliating an individual; or withholding regularly scheduled meals.
required_items.cite: RCG p.23; §6400.16. PART B: the regulation does not say 'written policy'. I included it because abuse prohibition, discipline and reporting are normal policy content.

required_items.text: The home shall immediately report abuse or suspected abuse of an individual 17 years of age or younger to ChildLine 1(800) 932-0313.

The home shall report the following incidents, alleged incidents and suspected incidents through the Department's information management system or on a form specified by the Department within 24 hours of discovery by a staff person: 1. Death. 2. A physical act by an individual in attempt to complete suicide. 3. Inpatient admission to a hospital. 4. Abuse, including individual to individual abuse. 5. Neglect. 6. Exploitation. 7. An individual who is missing for more than 24 hours or who could be in jeopardy if missing at all. 8. Law enforcement activity that occurs during the provision of a service or for which an individual is the subject of a law enforcement investigation that may lead to criminal charges against the individual. 9. Injury requiring treatment beyond first aid. 10. Fire requiring the services of the fire department not including false alarms. 11. Emergency closure. 12. Theft or misuse of individual funds. 13. A violation of individual rights.
required_items.cite: RCG p.24; §6400.18(a). PART B: the RCG says licensing staff verify through 'applicable policies' and calls incident policies and procedures an essential component.

required_items.text: The home shall report the following incidents, alleged incidents and suspected incidents through the Department's information management system or on a form specified by the Department within 72 hours of discovery by a staff person: 1. Use of restraint. A medication error as specified in §6400.167 (relating to medication errors), if the medication was ordered by a health care practitioner.
The individual and persons designated by the individual shall be notified within 24 hours of discovery of an incident relating to the individual.
required_items.cite: RCG p.25; §6400.18(c). 18d requires keeping documentation of the notification. PART B.

required_items.text: The incident report, or a summary of the incident, the finding, and the actions taken, redacted to exclude information about another individual and the reporter, unless the reporter is the individual who receives the report, shall be available to the individual and persons designated by the individual upon request.
The home shall take immediate action to protect the health, safety, and well-being of the individual following the initial knowledge or notice of an incident, alleged incident, or suspected incident.
The home shall initiate an investigation of an incident, alleged incident, or suspected incident within 24 hours of discovery by a staff person.
required_items.cite: RCG p.27; §6400.18(g). PART B. The RCG says providers must have access to a Certified Investigator at all times.

required_items.text: A Department-certified incident investigator shall conduct the investigation of the following incidents: 1. Death that occurs during the provision of service. 2. Inpatient admission to a hospital as a result of an accidental or unexplained injury or an injury caused by a staff person, another individual or during the use of a restraint. 3. Abuse. 4. Neglect. 5. Exploitation. 6. Injury requiring treatment beyond first aid as a result of an accidental or unexplained injury or an injury caused by a staff person, another individual or during the use of a restraint. 7. Theft or misuse of individual funds. 8. A violation of individual rights.

The home shall finalize the incident report through the Department's information management system or on a form specified by the Department within 30 days of discovery of the incident by a staff person unless the home notifies the Department in writing that an extension is necessary and the reason for the extension.
required_items.cite: RCG p.28; §6400.18(i). 18j(1)-(6) lists the required final-report contents. PART B.

required_items.text: The home shall review and analyze incidents and conduct and document a trend analysis at least every 3 months.
required_items.cite: RCG p.30; §6400.20(b). PART B. Related: 20a(1)-(3) cause analysis, corrective action and risk strategy for each confirmed incident; 20c(1)-(3) preventive measures; 20d educate staff and the individual; 20e monitor incidents and take actions to mitigate and manage risks.

required_items.text: (a) An application for a Pennsylvania criminal history record check shall be submitted to the State Police for prospective employees of the home who will have direct contact with individuals, including part-time and temporary staff persons who will have direct contact with individuals, within 5 working days after the person's date of hire. (b) If a prospective employee who will have direct contact with individuals resides outside this Commonwealth, an application for a Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) criminal history record check shall be submitted to the FBI in addition to the Pennsylvania criminal history record check within 5 working days after the person's date of hire. (c) The Pennsylvania and FBI criminal history record checks shall have been completed no more than 1 year prior to the person's date of hire.
required_items.cite: RCG pp.30-31; §6400.21(a)-(c). PART B (hiring/personnel policy content). The RCG says OAPSA standards supersede these timeframes. Providers must request checks on or before the first day of work and make a documented case-by-case hiring decision when a record exists.

required_items.text: The home shall inform and explain individual rights and the process to report a rights violation to the individual, and persons designated by the individual, upon admission to the home and annually thereafter.
required_items.cite: RCG p.52; §6400.34(a). PART B (individual rights content). 34b requires keeping the signed acknowledgment.

required_items.text: Program specialists and direct service workers shall be trained before working with individuals in: General fire safety, Evacuation procedures, Responsibilities during fire drills, The designated meeting place outside the building or within the fire safe area in the event of an actual fire, Smoking safety procedures if individuals or staff persons smoke at the home, The use of fire extinguishers, smoke detectors and fire alarms; and Notification of the local fire department as soon as possible after a fire is discovered.
required_items.cite: RCG p.56; §6400.46(a). PART B (training plan content). 46b-46d cover annual fire safety training, first aid, and first aid/Heimlich/CPR.

required_items.text: The orientation must encompass the following areas: 1. The application of: person-centered practices, community integration, individual choice, and supporting individuals to develop and maintain relationships. 2. The prevention, detection and reporting of abuse, suspected abuse and alleged abuse in accordance with the Older Adults Protective Services Act (35 P.S.§§ 10225.101-10225-5102), the Child Protective Service Law (23 Pa.C.S §§ 6301-6386), the Adult Protective Services Act (35 P.S. §§ 10210.101-10210.704) and applicable protective services regulations. 3. Individual rights. 4. Recognizing and reporting incidents. 5. Job-related knowledge and skills.
required_items.cite: RCG p.59; §6400.51(b). PART B (orientation plan). 51a lists who must complete orientation within 30 days of hire and before working alone.

required_items.text: The annual training hours specified in subsections (a) and (b) must encompass the following areas: 1. The application of person-centered practices, community integration, individual choice and supporting individuals to develop and maintain relationships. 2. The prevention, detection and reporting of abuse, suspected abuse and alleged abuse in accordance with the Older Adults Protective Services Act (35 P.S.§§ 10225.101-10225-5102), the Child Protective Service Law (23 Pa.C.S §§ 6301-6386), the Adult Protective Services Act (35 P.S. §§ 10210.101-10210.704) and applicable adult protective services regulations. 3. Individual rights. 4. Recognizing and reporting incidents. 5. The safe and appropriate use of behavior supports if the person works directly with an individual. 6. Implementation of the individual plan if the person works directly with an individual.
required_items.cite: RCG p.61; §6400.52 (the RCG labels this paragraph '6400.52(b)'). PART B (annual training plan). 52a requires 24 hours and 52b requires 12 hours by staff type. The RCG says the provider must establish the training-year dates in writing.

required_items.text: If an individual refuses routine medical or dental examination or treatment, the refusal and continued attempts to train the individual about the need for health care shall be documented in the individual's record.
required_items.cite: RCG p.92; §6400.143(a). PART B. The RCG says licensing staff review 'the provider's procedures for managing individuals' refusals'.

required_items.text: Prescription medications that are discontinued or expired shall be destroyed in a safe manner according to applicable Federal and State statutes and regulations.
required_items.cite: RCG p.100; §6400.163(h). PART B. The RCG says licensing staff review the provider's procedures for disposing of discontinued or expired medications. Medication administration (162, 163, 165-169) and the medication record (166a) are also reviewed in practice, and ODP requires medication administration training under 169.

sections: Home Serving Nine or More Individuals

official.notes: No single policy checklist was machine-readable, so this list is built from the regulation text in the RCG. The only dedicated checklist I found is ODP's 'NEW 6400 Policy Review List' (.docx), whose contents I could not read. It should override this list wherever the two differ. Part A is items the regulation itself says must be written: 22a/22b, 23, 33b, 103, 110h, 114a, 145, 192, and (homes serving 9+) 236 and 243. Part B is items marked 'PART B' in the cite field. In Part B the regulation does not say 'written policy', but the RCG says licensing staff verify them through 'applicable policies' and training records. They cover incident management, abuse and reporting, criminal-history hiring checks, rights notification, and the orientation and annual training topics. Organize the manual by the RCG section order above, using the regulation numbers as headings. Individual-level items are not provider policies and are not listed. They are the dental hygiene plan (142f-h), the behavior support component of the individual plan (195), the individual plan (185), and the individual emergency information (211). The Chapter 20 application and fees, the certificate of occupancy (14a), and the self-assessment (15) are paperwork, not policy content. Also not listed: the regulations' physical-site and fire-safety standards, which licensing staff check by observation of the home. The RCG also gives CEO and program specialist qualifications (43c, 44c) and staffing ratios (45). For waiver-funded Residential Habilitation, ODP provider enrollment adds requirements beyond Chapter 6400. These include Chapter 6100, the ODP Provider Applicant Orientation, the Waiver Provider Agreement and the New Provider Self-Assessment, and a 5-year manager experience rule for executive staff hired for enrollment. Those requirements are outside this list. The ODP licensing contact in the RCG is RA-odplicensing@pa.gov, and customer service is RA-customerservice@pa.gov or 1-888-565-9435.
